ANA.head: We leaned Anaheim’s way (58%), but Nashville had other ideas.

NSH.head: We had Nashville as slight underdogs (42%), and they pulled it off.

surprises.head: Nashville picked Anaheim’s defense apart
surprises.body: Anaheim usually gives up some of the league’s most dangerous shots. Even by those standards, this was a night of good looks: Nashville’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 9.8% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.4% (about 6.8% against Anaheim) and a league average of 6.4%. A team strays this far about once every 40 games.

surprises.head: Anaheim shut down Nashville’s power play
surprises.body: Nashville’s power play created 1.8 expected goals per 60, against their usual 7.8 (about 7.4 against Anaheim) and a league average of 7.7. A team strays this far about once every 25 games.

story.head: Josi reaches 800 points as the Predators beat the Ducks
paras: Cutter Gauthier got the scoring started for the Ducks midway through the first, his seventh straight game with a goal. Jayden Struble tied it 1-1 for Nashville 21 seconds later, and Nils Höglander put the Predators ahead for good late in the second. Shane Wright scored his first goal for Nashville midway through the third to make it 3-1, with Roman Josi picking up his 800th NHL point on the goal, and that goal turned out to be the winner. Mikael Granlund pulled the Ducks within one with less than eight minutes left, but that was as close as they got. Steven Stamkos added insurance with just under four minutes left. Wright finished with a goal and two assists.

The Ducks had a little more of the play, but the Predators had the finish. Justus Annunen made 27 saves for the Predators, and Laurent Brossoit stopped 18 of 22 at the other end. The Preds moved to 10-4-5 and climbed to second in the Central, while the Ducks fell to 10-8-1, third in the Pacific.
